newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania central bank to discuss monetary change.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania central bank to discuss monetary change.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said it will discuss on Thursday steps it will take this year to regain control of the monetary policy after it has been limited under the currency board regime.
"The board is due to discuss the monetary policy programme for 1997 and 1998," central bank deputy head Jonas Niaura told Reuters. The bank's board meets every Thursday.
"The discussion is connected to the restoration of the monetary policy functions to the Bank of Lithuania as a classical central bank," he added.

Under the currency board, the litas is pegged at four to one dollar and money supply is subordinated to the amount of hard currency reserves. The system deprives the central bank of powers to set the exchange rates or run a true monetary policy. The government wants to end the peg and eventually have a free-floating currency.
There has been confusion over government and central bank plans for the currency.

After he was elected in November, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius caused a run on the litas by saying he wanted to end the dollar peg at the start of this year. He later backtracked and mentioned an 18-month timetable.

Central bank experts have been working on the plans needed for it to become a full central bank and one policy aired by a bank official has been to link the litas to a basket consisting of the dollar and the mark.

But it has not been made clear whether the link to the basket was the central bank's end aim for the currency or whether this would be a stage for the currency on the way to its becoming freely-floating.
The currency board has brought stability to the litas and increased confidence in it but critics say it has led to an over-valued currency that is strangling exports.
